settings.title: Settings
settings.gameDirHint: Leave empty to detect automatically (Steam & standalone).
settings.steam: Open WTFTD with War Thunder from Steam
settings.steamHint: In Steam: War Thunder, Properties, General, Launch options: paste this line. Steam then starts the game and WTFTD with it (or brings the running one forward), and still counts your play time. Empty the field to stop.
settings.steamCopied: Copied: paste it in Steam's launch options
settings.dataHint: WTFTD keeps the game data of the sources ticked here, one or both. The one in use is picked with the Data button at the top. Update after a game patch.
source.keepFirst: Tick the other one first: the one in use goes once the other is kept

settings.removeDatamineHint: ≈1.2 GB your game data no longer uses. Downloaded again if you go back to the datamine.
source.gameHint: No download: WTFTD unpacks the game's own files on this PC (≈650 MB on disk, about 3 minutes). Always your game's exact version, works offline.
source.datamineHint: ≈1 GB from GitHub with Git, a few minutes. Works without the game. Community data, not Gaijin's: it can be ahead of or behind your game.
source.issue.python: Not available here: reading the game files needs Python 3.14 or newer.
source.issue.game: Not available yet: War Thunder wasn't found. Set its folder in Settings.
settings.howtoText: WTFTD writes a mission file into War Thunder's UserMissions folder. Start the game, open Single missions → User missions and pick it.
onboard.title: Welcome to WTFTD
onboard.text: First launch: WTFTD needs the game data to build its database on your PC. Choose where it comes from:
onboard.lead: Here is what it will do:
onboard.wait: Keep this window open: WTFTD takes care of the rest.
onboard.buttonGame: Accept and read the game files
onboard.whereApp: Its own folder: {path} (the game database, its copy of the game data, your settings and library).
onboard.whereGame: War Thunder's folder ({path}): only the missions you create (UserMissions) and, for custom vehicles, new files in content/pkg_local and pkg_user. Nothing of the game itself is changed.
onboard.whereRemove: Settings → Uninstall WTFTD removes all of it.
onboard.sources: What it downloads, and from where
onboard.srcData: {url}: the game's files, from the community War Thunder datamine (not Gaijin's), ≈1 GB with Git now; then checked every 3 hours and updated after game patches.
onboard.srcDataGame: Nothing for the game data: it comes from your War Thunder folder (read only), and is checked every 3 hours and rebuilt after game patches.
onboard.srcGit: {url}: portable Git (MinGit, ≈40 MB), only if Git isn't installed.
onboard.srcImages: {a} (War Thunder's official encyclopedia) and {b}: vehicle, shell and flag pictures, as you browse (the datamine's own pictures when they have none).
onboard.srcApp: {url}: only checks whether a newer WTFTD is out.
onboard.srcNone: No account, no tracking: nothing else is downloaded, nothing about you is sent.
onboard.gameNotFound: not found yet: set it in Settings
preview.title: Mission file preview
mods.off: Enable custom vehicles in Settings to modify stats.
mods.note: Custom vehicle: the mission uses a copy of this vehicle loaded in place of “{host}” (a vehicle you own). Only one custom vehicle per type at a time — the last mission you create defines it.
toast.cdkRemoved: Removed {n} custom vehicle file(s) from the game folder
settings.cdkHint: Uses War Thunder's userVehicles mechanism (content/pkg_local): your vehicle is loaded in place of a host vehicle you own, so missions work without buying it. Only new files are written; nothing replaces game files. Not endorsed by Gaijin — use at your own risk.
settings.hostsHint: Host vehicles must be owned (reserve vehicles are). With “New custom aircraft”, aircraft and helicopters don't need a host.
uninstall.title: Uninstall WTFTD
uninstall.settingsHint: Remove what WTFTD put on this PC: everything, or only some parts.
uninstall.hint: Choose what to remove from this PC.
uninstall.loading: Looking at what WTFTD put on this PC…
uninstall.allHint: Every part below: nothing of WTFTD is left.
uninstall.cdk: Custom vehicle files in the game
uninstall.cdkHint: {n} file(s) WTFTD added to the game's content folder. Missions with custom vehicles stop working.
uninstall.missionsHint: {n} mission(s) in the game's UserMissions folder (other missions are kept).
uninstall.cacheHint: {size}: WTFTD's copy of the game files, pictures, maps. Made again when needed.
uninstall.dataHint: {size}: vehicles, weapons and maps read from the game files. Built again at the next launch.
uninstall.userHint: {size}: settings, My vehicles, My maps, My missions, the history of What changed, My hangar, the results of the Test bench. Gone for good: share what you want to keep first.
uninstall.appSource: WTFTD runs from its source code here: delete its folder yourself to remove it.
uninstall.appMac: macOS runs WTFTD from a temporary copy (it was opened straight from Downloads): move WTFTD.app to the Trash yourself.
uninstall.gameSafe: War Thunder itself is never touched: only what WTFTD added to it goes, and the one line of config.blk if you turned sound mods on.
uninstall.workingHint: This can take a minute: the cache holds thousands of files. WTFTD is working, don't close it.
uninstall.bye: WTFTD has been removed from this PC.
uninstall.byeHint: This window closes in a moment; the app and its folder go a few seconds later. Thanks for using WTFTD!
mods.noteAir: Custom aircraft: WTFTD creates a new aircraft (copy of this one with your changes) in content/pkg_user — no host needed. Experimental.
cheat.immortalHint: Your vehicle can’t be destroyed. With custom vehicles its damage model is made 1000× tougher; ground vehicles and ships are also repaired instantly.
cheat.noOverloadHint: No wings torn off by overspeed or g; gear, flaps and canopy don't break either (custom vehicles: the flight model's limits are raised).
cheat.superMobilityHint: Ground vehicles: engine power ×4, top speed ×2, brakes ×3. Aircraft: much faster roll and pitch, tighter turns (more lift, bigger and quicker controls, less inertia), half the drag, engine power / thrust ×3, 40 % lighter; pair it with Unbreakable airframe. Custom vehicles; a value set under Modifications wins.
cheat.infAmmoHint: The game refills your ammo when you run out.
cheat.noReloadHint: Instant rearm, and near-instant reload on every gun.
cheat.noReloadCdk: (Gun reload needs custom vehicles — only rearm is instant now.)
cheat.passiveHint: Enemy units of the scenario can't fire.
cheat.hostileHint: Enemy units that hold their fire in the scenario (test-drive targets) fire at will. Units set in the map editor keep their setting.
cheat.targetsBackHint: Destroyed targets of the scenario and the ones added in the map editor are repaired and brought back every 20 s.
cheat.hotkeysHint: Switch options while you play with the game's Quick radio messages (give them keys in the game's controls): #1 invulnerable, #2 no reload, #3 passive targets, #4 repair, #5 targets back, #6 back to the start, #9 help.
hk.help: WTFTD keys (Quick radio messages): #1 invulnerable · #2 no reload · #3 passive targets · #4 repair · #5 targets back · #6 back to the start · #9 this help
hk.intro: WTFTD keys: Quick radio message #9 shows them
cheat.repairHint: Fully repairs and rearms your vehicle every N seconds.
settings.autoUpdate: Update automatically when the game is patched (checks every 3 h)
bt.title: Battle
bt.hint: The game's chat and battle log, live. WTFTD only reads them, nothing is sent anywhere.
lim.title: Breaking limits
ov.profileNew: New overlay for an aircraft or a type
ov.noSuch: Pick an aircraft or a type from the list
ov.profileHint: An aircraft's own overlay comes first, then its type's, then the one for all aircraft. A new one starts as a copy of what you see here.
bn.title: Test bench
bn.hint: Hard numbers instead of the stat card: you fly a guided test, WTFTD reads the results from the game and keeps only the valid stretches. It sends nothing to the game: you do the flying.
bn.noCurve: Tick runs in the table to lay them over each other.
bn.empty: No result for this test yet.
bn.d.top: Level flight at full power, until the speed stops rising
bn.d.climb: Climb rate by altitude, time to altitude
bn.d.turn: 360° time, radius and G at a held speed
bn.d.bleed: Speed lost in half a circle
bn.d.stall: The slowest level flight, engine at idle
bn.do.top: Hold {altitude} with the wings level, gear and flaps up, throttle at maximum (War Emergency Power or afterburner if the aircraft has it). Fly straight until the speed stops rising: 20 steady seconds make a result. For another altitude, go there and do the same. Leave the mission when you are done.
bn.do.climb: Full throttle, gear and flaps up, wings level. Climb at a steady {speed} and keep that speed all the way up: the result follows the climb until you stop. Leave the mission when you are done.
bn.do.turn: At {altitude} and {speed}: full throttle, gear and flaps up. Bank into a level turn and hold the height and the speed for at least one full circle. For another speed, start again at that speed. Leave the mission when you are done.
bn.do.accel: Fly level at {altitude}, below {from}, gear and flaps up. Open the throttle fully and stay level with the wings level until you pass {to}. Leave the mission when you are done.
bn.do.bleed: Fly level at {altitude} and {speed}, full throttle, gear and flaps up. Pull as hard as the aircraft allows through half a circle, keeping the height. Several tries are fine: the best one stays. Leave the mission when you are done.
bn.do.stall: Fly level at {altitude}. Throttle to idle, gear and flaps up, wings level. Raise the nose little by little to hold the height, and let the speed fall gently until the aircraft starts to sink. Leave the mission when you are done.
bn.alteredHint: This aircraft's setup has modifications or cheats: the mission uses them, and its results stay apart from the real aircraft.
bn.badField: Check the test's numbers: the second speed must be above the first.
bn.why.moving: The speed never settled: stay level until it stops moving.
bn.why.heading: The game gave no heading, so the turn can't be timed.
bn.why.speed: The speed changed during the circle.
bn.why.late: The throttle was opened too late: the run began at {v} km/h.
bn.why.entry: The turn began at {v} km/h, too far from the speed asked.
bn.why.soft: No hard pull: it takes 2.5 G or more through half a circle.
bn.why.notLevel: The aircraft wasn't in level flight before it sank.
bn.why.rate: The speed fell {v} km/h each second: let it fall gently.
bn.why.pulled: {v} G at the end: let the aircraft slow down, don't pull.
bn.why.noStall: Level flight held down to {v} km/h: the aircraft never started to sink.
bn.idle: Create a mission above, then fly it: WTFTD records by itself and finds the valid stretches when you leave. The mission's description in the game says what to do.
bn.paused: Game paused: this time doesn't count
bn.waiting: Mission ready: in the game, Single missions, User missions, {title}
bn.cardKey: Dashed line or diamond: the game's stat card
bn.damaged: The test bench file couldn't be read: it was kept aside as bench.bad.json.
fl.title: Flight data
fl.hint: What the game reports while you fly, as curves: pick the values under the chart. Record a flight to a CSV file that opens in Excel, then replay it here. Recording keeps going from the hangar to the next flight until you stop it.
fl.empty: Nothing to show yet. Fly, and the curves start by themselves while this tab is open.
fl.rep.title: Flight report
fl.rep.note: Hover a value for the speed and altitude it happened at. Sustained turn: level (under 2 m/s of climb), speed steady (under 0.5 m/s² of acceleration), over 1.5 G, for 3 s or more. Times to climb count from the start of the log.
ov.title: My overlay
ov.hint: What you see and hear in flight: a small click-through window over the game, and beeps near your aircraft's breaking speeds. It only reads the game's local data; nothing is added to the game. Changes apply at once.
ov.enable: Turn on the overlay and alarms
ov.onScreen: Show it on my screen now (sample values)
ov.dragHint: Your screen, to scale: drag the text to place it. Sample values here; in flight you get the real ones.
ov.linesHint: Write what you like. Values go between braces: click one below to add it to the line you're editing. {mach:3} sets the decimals, {turn_pct:bar} draws a % as a gauge, and any field the game sends works under its own name, like {RPM 2}.
ov.hudHint: A fighter's head-up display drawn from your own aircraft's numbers: heading, pitch ladder, flight path, speed and altitude. It isn't lined up with the game's horizon: WTFTD can't know where the game's camera looks.
ov.hudKeyHint: Switches the HUD between its two places: the game doesn't say which view you're in.
ov.mapHint: The game's own map, your aircraft, its trail and what never moves: airfields, capture zones, bases, and the way to your nearest airfield. Never another aircraft or vehicle: enemies on an overlay can count as cheating for Gaijin.
ov.mapUp.heading: Your nose
ov.mapAlliesHint: Told apart by their colour only, the game doesn't say a unit's team or who's an AI: blue, or a squadmate's green. In an air battle the vehicles and ships are the AI. Enemies never show.
ov.bgPick: Use a screenshot of the game
ov.bgHint: Take a screenshot in flight and pick it here, or paste it with Ctrl+V: you then place the text on your real HUD. Without one, this is an outline of the HUD on a 16:9 screen.
ov.show: Show the window in flight (off: beeps only)
ov.hideCrash: Hide the overlay after a crash (the beeps always stop)
ov.hideUnknown: Hide the overlay while the aircraft is unknown
ov.soundFocus: Beep only when the game is in front
ov.soundEngine: No beeps with the engines stopped
ov.holdKey: Key to hold to hide the overlay
ov.hideNA: Hide when a value is N/A
ov.blocksHint: More text in other places of the screen: drag the blocks on the picture, add a line to one here, or pick a line's block in the Lines tab.
mods.voiceHint: The crew speaks the language of its country when the game's Crew language is on Auto (outside arcade) or Crew country. Special voices need the game's Use special crew voice-over.
ov.pctAlways: Gear and flaps % even when retracted
settings.closeWithGame: Close WTFTD when the game closes
settings.launchGame: Launch War Thunder when WTFTD opens, if it isn't running yet
ov.hotkeyPh: Click here, then press a key, a mouse button or a joystick button
ov.hotkeyHint: Works with the game in front. Esc removes the key.
ov.tryHint: Move it: the overlay shows on your screen and beeps as in flight. Only this alarm reacts.
ov.part.name: Name
ov.sheetKey: Key to hold for the aircraft's sheet
ov.v.heading: Heading
update.available: The game was patched ({v}): WTFTD's data is older
update.rebuild: WTFTD was updated: its game data needs rebuilding ({v})
update.ahead: Your game data comes from the community datamine ({data}), ahead of your game ({game}): its vehicles and BRs are the dev server's.
theme.label: Theme
cheat.crewHint: Max crew skills, plus the expert / ace qualification events use. Untested in user missions.
editor.title: Scenario editor
editor.intro: Move, add or remove allies and enemies on the real map of the scenario, and choose how they behave.
editor.hintSelect: Click: select · Ctrl/Shift+click: several · Shift+drag: an area · drag to move · Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V: copy / paste · Del: remove · ZQSD / WASD: move the map · wheel: zoom · right click: actions
editor.zonePlayer: The scenario puts you here (at start or after a crash). Your start, set under You, moves this zone with it.
editor.zoneUnits: The scenario brings these units here (at start or while the mission runs, sometimes a few picked at random among them):
editor.pasteClick: Click on the map to paste the copied units there (Esc: cancel)
editor.copied: {n} unit(s) copied: Ctrl+V pastes them under the pointer
editor.addN: How many units each click places
editor.multiHint: Ctrl/Shift+click a unit (map or list) to add or remove it, Shift+drag on the map to select an area. Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V copy and paste, Ctrl+D duplicates, Del removes.
editor.multiMoveHint: Hunts me: enemies only · Escorts me: allies only · Stays still: not aircraft.
editor.noMine: No saved vehicle of this kind: save one from its panel (disk icon), it can then be used here, its loadout included.
ai.title: AI unit's loadout
ai.hint: Weapons and ammo of this unit of the map editor, as for your own vehicle. Apply to go back to the editor.
editor.hintAdd: Click on the map to place a new enemy
editor.hintAddAsset: Click on the map to place an asset
editor.noSel: Select a unit on the map or in the list.
editor.noUnits: This scenario has no editable unit (its targets come from the game's templates). You can still add units.
editor.playerHint: Drag your marker on the map to move your start. Height is above sea level.
editor.heightHint: No heightmap for this map: estimated from the nearest unit; raise it if the vehicle spawns underground.
editor.removedHint: This unit is removed from the mission.
loadout.copyPreset: Click to copy this preset into your custom loadout
loadout.useSaved: Click to load this saved loadout into your custom loadout
loadout.gridHint: Rows are the official presets, columns the pylons — click a row to use it. Turn on the custom loadout to fill each pylon yourself.
loadout.legacyHint: This aircraft only has the game's fixed presets, laid out like in the hangar: click a row to use it.
loadout.pickHint: Click a pylon of the Custom row to choose what it carries.
loadout.dragHint: Drag a weapon onto a pylon of the Custom row to copy it there, from any row. Hold Ctrl to swap two pylons of the Custom row instead.
loadout.more: {n} more — refine with the filter or a category
need.radar: This aircraft has no radar-guided weapon: the missile may never lock.
need.laser: No laser designator on this aircraft: add a targeting pod or it won't guide.
need.saclos: This aircraft has no missile guidance system: the missile will fly unguided.
need.tv: This aircraft has no TV / IR guided weapon: lock-on may not work.
editor.noMap: No map background for this scenario yet: play it once with WTFTD open and its tactical map is captured from the game.
editor.tplNote: This unit comes from one of the game's templates: it can't be moved or changed, but you can remove it, freeze it, make it passive or make it hunt you.
editor.tplNoteSwap: This unit comes from one of the game's templates: it can't be moved, but you can change its vehicle (the mission then declares that template's units itself), remove it, freeze it, make it passive or make it hunt you.
cond.startMoved: Where and how you start (ground or air, altitude, speed, heading) is set on the map: Maps → a map → Edit on the map → You.
editor.heading: Heading
editor.headingHint: Or drag the arrow's tip on the map.
editor.zoneUsed: The scenario's scripts use this zone (spawns, respawns, targets): moving it moves what appears there.
editor.zoneUnused: No script of the scenario seems to use this zone.
editor.runtimeNote: The scenario picks its spot when the mission runs (often at random among several zones): it isn't shown on the map.
editor.runtimeZones: Where it may appear: {n} zone(s), circled on the map.
editor.auto.title: Vehicles by BR
editor.auto.hint: Each unit gets a vehicle of its own kind (fighter, bomber, tank, SPAA…) at the closest BR. Template units keep theirs.
editor.auto.done: {n} unit(s) changed to vehicles near BR {br}
editor.auto.fireHint: The test flights' and test drives' targets are passive: Attacks makes them fire at you.
editor.auto.followHint: Follows the vehicle you take: when its BR changes, these units get vehicles near the new one (editor opened, mission created).
editor.auto.followed: {n} unit(s) follow your vehicle: vehicles near BR {br}
editor.areaNote: Shown where the scenario moves it at start ({area}).
editor.hintAddAlly: Click on the map to place a new ally
editor.noOodle: Map background unavailable: the game's maps are Oodle-compressed and no Oodle runtime (oo2core_*_win64.dll / liboo2core*.dylib, shipped with many games) was found on this PC. Set one in Settings, or play this scenario once with WTFTD open to capture its map.
editor.mapError: The map background could not be read from the game files.
editor.map3dHint: The real map in 3D, read from your game. Right drag to turn · wheel to zoom
editor.hintRoute: Click on the map to add a point · drag a point to move it · right click or Esc to finish
editor.waveHint: The lowest wave is there at the start, each next one comes when the one before is destroyed. {cheat} leaves them alone.
editor.followHint: Follows you around and engages enemies on its way.
editor.movesHint: This unit follows a route in the scenario: moving it changes where the route starts.
cond.fuelHint: Share of the tanks filled at spawn. "Unlimited fuel" (Cheats) overrides it.
settings.oodleHint: The game's tactical maps are Oodle-compressed. WTFTD uses an oo2core_<n>_win64.dll / liboo2core*.dylib found in your other games (Steam / Epic folders). Leave empty for automatic.
editor.playerHintAir: Drag your marker to start somewhere else: you then start in the air, at the altitude below (above sea level).
editor.spawnRunway: The scenario spawns you on this runway (dashed line), whatever the position written in the mission.
editor.spawnArea: The scenario places you here when the mission starts.
editor.spawnMoved: Moved: the scenario's runway / start point is no longer used.
editor.tpStart: The scenario moves this unit here when the mission starts.
editor.tpStartMoved: Moved: the scenario no longer teleports it at start.
editor.tpLater: When destroyed, it respawns at the circled point.
settings.languageHint: Translations other than English were machine-assisted and may contain mistakes — corrections are welcome on GitHub.
stats.title: Performance
filters.statsPickType: Pick a vehicle type to filter by all its stats.
path.title: Research path
path.note: Research (RP) and purchase (SL) cost of each vehicle along the line. Modules, crew training and the rank requirements are not counted. The last column is each vehicle's reward in research points.
wpick.title: Choose weapons
wpick.hint: Click weapons to select them: vehicles must carry all of them.
share.title: Share
share.text: Send this code to a friend: in WTFTD they click Import and paste it (or send them the .wtftd file). It goes to their My vehicles, My maps or My missions.
share.importText: Paste the code a friend sent you, or open a .wtftd file (you can also drop it on the window).
share.invalid: This is not a WTFTD code.
share.unknownVehicle: This vehicle isn't in your game data ({id}): update the game data in Settings.
share.setupsHint: Your saved vehicle setups (loadout, ammo, modifications, cheats) and the ones friends shared (Import). Choose puts one in the bottom bar.
model.loading: Reading the model from your game...
model.none: This model can't be read from your game files.
model.hint: Drag to turn · wheel to zoom. Read from your own game files.
compare.max: Up to {n} vehicles in a comparison
compare.title: Vehicle comparison
app.newVersionHint: You have {v}. Download the new version from the release page.
app.feedbackHint: Found a bug or have an idea? Tell us on GitHub (a free account is needed).
app.feedbackHow: GitHub opens with the form filled in: you read it, then send it yourself (a free account is needed). Issues are public.
app.supportHint: WTFTD is free. If you enjoy it, you can buy me a coffee on Ko-fi ❤
upg.label: Upgrades
upg.estimated: Stock aircraft performance (speed, climb, turn) is estimated from the modules' effects.
mymaps.title: My maps
mymaps.hint: Your saved map variants (Maps → a map → Save…) and the ones friends shared (Import).
mymaps.empty: No saved map yet: in Maps, edit a variant, then Save….
combo.empty: No saved mission yet: pick a vehicle and a map, then the save button of the bottom bar.
combo.needBoth: Pick a vehicle and a map first.
share.unknownMap: This map isn't in your game data ({id}): update them in Settings.
share.noSetup: This mission has no saved setup (made with an older WTFTD).
share.importedHint.vehicle: Find it in My vehicles: Choose puts it in the bottom bar.
share.importedHint.map: Find it in My maps: Choose makes it the mission's map.
share.importedHint.mission: Find it in My missions: Create mission, or Choose to change it first.
maps.title: Maps & scenarios
maps.hint: A mission is a vehicle and a map: pick them in any order, then Create mission. The vehicle's setup (loadout, ammo, cheats…) stays in its panel.
maps.othersHint: Beta: a bare start (you alone, no targets) placed where the game's own missions put that kind of vehicle. Add units with Edit on the map.
maps.battlesHint: Beta: the game's Domination layouts. You start at one side's spawn; the capture zones and the other side's spawn are shown in the editor. No AI, score or capture: add units with Edit on the map.
maps.dialogHint: Choose a variant for your mission. Edit on the map moves, adds or removes its units, as in the vehicle panel.
mission.title: Mission
mission.hint: These belong to the mission (vehicle + map). Title and file name stay automatic until you change them.
mission.diffInGame: Chosen in the game at launch
mission.diffHint: Picked here, the game no longer asks at launch and the mission keeps these settings. ● marks a setting changed from the game's preset.
mapset.title: Settings of {name}
mapset.hint: They belong to the map: they go with any vehicle, and into the variant when you save it.
mapset.pickFirst: Choose a variant to set its targets, enemies, time and weather.
pick.switched: {map} doesn't suit this vehicle: {other} picked instead.
arm.title: Weapons
arm.hint: Every missile, bomb, rocket and torpedo in the game: stats from the game files, what each one is best at, comparison and the vehicles that carry it.
arm.noData: Weapon data isn't built yet: update the game data (Settings → Update game data).
arm.guideHint: Rankings are computed from the game files' stats only. Real performance also depends on the launch platform (radar, speed, altitude) and on game patches.
arm.fh.ccm: Counter-countermeasures: the seeker can reject flares
arm.fh.act: Own radar: no need to keep the target locked after launch
arm.fh.ins: Inertial guidance: flies toward the predicted target position before its seeker locks
arm.fh.dl: Datalink: the launcher's radar updates the missile in flight
arm.fh.loft: Climbs after launch to fly higher and further
arm.fh.ff: No need to guide or designate after launch
arm.fh.wire: Wire-guided: limited by wire length, unaffected by jamming
arm.base.title: Bombing a target
arm.base.note: The game's own values: the target's HP by the battle's BR (its mission templates), and what an explosion takes off by its TNT equivalent (its explosion table). That table isn't proportional: several small bombs do more than one big one of the same weight. Every weapon must land in the target's zone. Not counted: fires after the hit, maps that set their own values, and airfields on maps without bases (+20 %).
arm.colh.hit: What one of these takes off a target: the game's explosion table, from its TNT equivalent
arm.colh.need: How many of these destroy the target chosen above, all landing in its zone
arm.colh.napalm: Napalm and incendiary bombs hurt a bombing zone through their own multiplier (× {n}), not by the explosion table: no count
arm.col.name: Weapon
arm.colh.v: Speed the motor adds to the launch speed, from thrust, burn time and mass (no drag). Mach for missiles, m/s for rockets and ATGMs (cruise speed), knots for torpedoes
arm.colh.gl: Maximum load factor: how hard the missile can turn
arm.colh.ob: Off-boresight: how far off your nose the seeker can lock a target
arm.colh.trk: Seeker tracking rate: how fast a crossing target it can follow
arm.colh.lk: IR lock range on a target's engine exhaust (rear aspect)
arm.colh.aa: IR lock range from the front / side (all-aspect). Empty = rear-aspect only
arm.colh.tnt: Explosive mass × the explosive's strength, in kg of TNT: what matters for blast damage
arm.colh.br: Lowest battle rating (RB) of the vehicles that carry it
arm.colh.nv: Number of vehicles that carry it
arm.useh.dogfight: Max G, lock angle, seeker tracking rate, IRCCM, all-aspect lock
arm.useh.aspect: All-aspect lock range first, then speed, range and G
arm.useh.flares: IRCCM first, then tracking rate and G
arm.useh.bvr: Range, speed, active seeker, datalink, loft
arm.useh.ff: Needs no guidance after launch, then seeker range and agility
arm.useh.close: Max G, lock angle and acceleration off the rail
arm.useh.agile: Max G, speed and proximity fuse radius
arm.useh.tank: Penetration first, then speed and explosive
arm.useh.eff: TNT equivalent divided by the weapon's mass
arm.guide.aam_ir:
Dogfight: high G, a wide lock angle (off-boresight, best with a helmet sight) and a fast-tracking seeker win turning fights.
All-aspect missiles can lock a target from the front; rear-aspect ones only see the engine exhaust: fire behind the target.
IRCCM rejects flares: very valuable against modern aircraft that flare constantly.
The engine burn time and top speed decide how far the missile really reaches; range in the files is a best case.
Launch close and behind a non-maneuvering target for the best hit chance, and keep the target away from the sun.
arm.guide.aam_radar:
Semi-active (SARH) missiles need your radar to keep the lock until impact: you keep flying toward the enemy.
Active (ARH) missiles turn on their own radar near the target: fire, turn away, engage the next one.
Inertial guidance + datalink let you launch from long range; lofting climbs high and keeps energy for the end.
Radar missiles can be defeated by chaff and by the target flying perpendicular to you (notching): launch on targets flying toward or away from you.
For close range, prefer high-G missiles or an IR missile.
arm.guide.sam:
Fast missiles with high G reach maneuvering aircraft and helicopters before they can react.
SACLOS missiles need you to keep the crosshair (or radar track) on the target until impact; IR and active ones are fire & forget.
A large proximity fuse radius helps against small, agile targets like helicopters and drones.
Range decides how far you can hit attackers before they release their weapons.
arm.guide.atgm:
Penetration decides what you can kill from the front; tandem warheads defeat explosive reactive armor (ERA).
SACLOS / beam riders need you to keep aiming until impact: you stay exposed. Fire & forget (IR / TV / radar) lets you hide right after launch.
Fast missiles leave less time for the target to hide or shoot back; slow ones can be shot down by active protection systems.
On helicopters, long range lets you stay out of reach of SPAA.
arm.guide.agm:
TV / IR seekers are fire & forget: lock, launch, and you're free to leave. Laser needs the target designated until impact.
Anti-radiation missiles home on radars (SPAA and ships); radar-guided anti-ship missiles are made for ships.
Heavier warheads (TNT equivalent) kill tanks and destroy bases without a direct hit; penetration matters for small missiles on armored targets.
Long range lets you stay out of reach of air defenses.
arm.guide.gbomb:
Laser-guided bombs need the target designated (pod or another aircraft) until impact; GPS / INS and TV / IR ones are fire & forget.
Release high and fast to glide further: the further the target, the more energy you need.
TNT equivalent decides how close the impact must be to kill a tank or destroy a base.
arm.guide.bomb:
TNT equivalent is what kills: a near miss with a big bomb destroys a tank, a small one needs a direct hit.
Bases and airfields need a total TNT amount: big bombs reach it in fewer drops.
High-drag (retarded) bombs let you drop low and fast without being caught in the blast.
Heavier loads slow your aircraft: pick the lightest load that does the job.
arm.guide.rocket:
Against tanks, penetration matters: HEAT rockets go through roofs and sides, and hit-to-kill AP rockets work on light armor.
HE rockets with a big warhead are good against light vehicles, AA and soft targets.
Fast rockets are easier to aim at range; fire in salvos for a better chance to hit.
arm.guide.torpedo:
Speed reduces the time a ship has to turn away; range lets you launch from a safe distance.
The TNT equivalent decides how many torpedoes a large ship needs.
Check the launch limits in game (maximum speed and altitude for aircraft).
arm.note.su_r_73: A dogfight favourite: turns very hard and locks far off your nose, best with a helmet sight. Its IRCCM narrows the seeker, so flares still work head-on or from behind. Weaker at range.
arm.note.us_aim9m_sidewinder: Often called the best flare rejection among older IR missiles: it pauses when it sees flares, then looks again, so the target must flare and turn. Without a helmet sight it can't take wide-angle shots.
arm.note.fr_r_550_magic_2: Grouped with the R-73 as a strong short-range missile: narrow seeker view and good off-boresight shots.
arm.note.us_aim9l_sidewinder: The benchmark early all-aspect missile, carried by a huge number of aircraft. No IRCCM: flares plus a turn defeat it.
arm.note.su_r_27er: Widely seen as the strongest semi-active missile: fast, high G, it often wins long-range duels even fired second. Like every SARH missile, it's lost if your radar drops the lock. Its flight model is due for a rework.
arm.note.us_aim7m_sparrow: The standard NATO semi-active missile. Reliable, but generally rated below the R-27ER. Recently given a new flight model.
arm.note.us_aim7f_sparrow: A long guidance time helps at high altitude and speed; otherwise plays like the AIM-7M.
arm.note.uk_skyflash_temp: Very fast but with a short motor burn: excellent up close, mediocre past about 10 km.
arm.note.il_aspide_1a: Fast semi-active missile; works best on targets above you, where the ground doesn't confuse the radar.
arm.note.us_aim_120a: Fast, short time of flight, good at every range; some players find it inconsistent at holding lock. Buffed in the September 2026 update (better turning at low speed, smaller warhead).
arm.note.us_aim_120b: Plays like the AIM-120A: a fast, fire & forget all-rounder. Buffed in the September 2026 update.
arm.note.fr_mica_em: Seen as the hardest active missile to notch and very deadly up close; it bleeds speed when maneuvering at long range. Reworked in September 2026 (single-stage motor, longer range).
arm.note.su_r_77: Soviet active-radar missile; most players find it plays about like the AIM-120A/B.
arm.note.su_r_77_1: Some players call it the best all-round active missile, close to the MICA on wide-angle shots.
arm.note.cn_pl12: China's long-range active missile; its autopilot was reworked in 2026.
arm.note.cn_pl12a: Heavier than the PL-12 with more thrust and a longer burn since an April 2026 update.
arm.note.jp_aam4: Japan's long-range active missile; tuned several times in 2026.
arm.note.us_aim_54c: Rebuilt in June 2026: thrust changes with altitude, very high top speed. Made for very long shots on big, non-maneuvering targets.
arm.note.152mm_zur_9m311: Fast missile backed by 30 mm guns on the Tunguska; its radar only covers the front, and players rate it below newer systems.
arm.note.160mm_sam_1c: IR missiles that pull enough G to catch maneuvering attack jets and are described as very hard to flare. Short reach.
arm.note.239mm_9m331: Strong radar-command SAM (Tor); opinions differ on how hard it is to dodge.
arm.note.152mm_mim146: ADATS: proximity fuse and good reach against helicopters, but only 8 missiles on a slow, big vehicle.
arm.note.165mm_vt_1: Very strong inside about 8 km, loses agility beyond that.
arm.note.us_iris_t_sl: Early complaints were about limited speed and range against stand-off missiles like the Kh-38; its seeker was changed in late 2025.
arm.note.us_starstreak: Given a new flight model and fully physical guidance in March 2026; it was considered weak before.
arm.note.130mm_starstreak_hvm: Given a new flight model and fully physical guidance in March 2026; it was considered weak before.
arm.note.70mm_fim_92e: Short-range IR missile that locks late (under about 2 km). Flares alone only throw it off briefly: the pilot must also turn away.
arm.note.su_9m127: Long reach and a proximity fuse, so it also hits helicopters and aircraft: flexible. Rated good but not the best; its penetration was reduced.
arm.note.us_hellfire_agm_114_k: Big warhead and good penetration, but laser-guided: you keep the target designated until impact. Slow enough for SPAA to shoot down.
arm.note.spike_er: Fire & forget: launch, hide, engage the next target. Slow, and players often complain it hits barrels or breeches instead of the roof.
arm.note.110mm_spike_lr2: Fire & forget top-attack missile; slow, and damage on top hits can be inconsistent.
arm.note.euro_atgw3: Fire & forget and faster than the Spike; the Tiger that carries it is considered weak overall.
arm.note.130mm_9m120: Much faster than slow fire & forget missiles, with less reach and damage.
arm.note.lmur: Very long reach; not fully fire & forget against moving targets. The Mi-28NM carrying it is rated among the best top-tier helicopters.
arm.note.152mm_9m133: The standard Soviet heavy ATGM for tanks and IFVs: high penetration and long range.
arm.note.127mm_tow_2b: Top-attack missile; players complain about inconsistent damage when it strikes from above.
arm.note.us_agm_65b: Locks before launch then guides itself: very accurate, one or two hits kill a heavy tank. TV seeker: daylight only.
arm.note.us_agm_65d: Infrared Maverick: fire & forget like the TV versions, and it also works at night.
arm.note.uk_brimstone_dm: In game it's laser-guided with terminal homing only; its real radar fire & forget mode isn't modeled.
arm.note.su_kh_38mt: The most debated weapon in ground battles: long reach, thermal seeker, fire & forget, often launched from beyond SPAA range. Tuned in September 2025, still controversial.
arm.note.su_kh_29t: Huge warhead that can kill several vehicles at once; TV seeker, fire & forget.
arm.note.su_kh_29l: Huge warhead like the Kh-29T, but laser-guided: the target must stay designated.
arm.note.fr_as30l: Laser-guided with good reach and damage; seen as the Maverick's main rival around its BR.
arm.note.us_agm_88c: Anti-radiation missile: homes on enemy radars (SPAA, ships).
arm.note.us_gbu_12_paveway_2: Cheap, reliable 500 lb laser-guided bomb; keep the laser on the target until it lands.
arm.note.us_gbu_10_paveway_2: 2000 lb laser-guided bomb: kills several tanks or hard targets at once.
arm.note.us_2000lb_gbu_24: 2000 lb laser-guided bomb with a longer glide; the EGBU-24 adds GPS.
arm.note.us_gbu_39: Small glide bomb carried in large numbers, long glide range; release is capped at Mach 1.1.
arm.note.su_kab_500kr: TV-guided, fire & forget after lock, daylight only. Players say it locks much closer in game than in reality, and its warhead is about half a FAB-500's.
arm.note.su_kab_1500l: Very large laser-guided bomb that kills tanks over a wide area.
arm.note.fr_250kg_aasm_250_hammer_gps: Long-reach, rocket-boosted precision bomb; release limited to Mach 1 since September 2026.
arm.note.il_spice_1000: Long-reach precision glide bomb on Israeli jets.
arm.note.su_fab500sh: 500 kg bombs are the workhorse for killing tanks: much more forgiving than 250 kg (about 12 m destruction radius measured by players).
arm.note.us_2000lb_mk_84_ldgp: Big blast radius: kills several tanks bunched together and does heavy base damage.
arm.note.de_sc1800b: Base killer: one destroys a standard base on its own, a double-health base needs two.
arm.note.su_fab5000: Huge bomb for bases and airfields, with a very wide armor-destroying radius.
arm.note.de_sc2500: Huge base and airfield killer with a wide armor-destroying radius.
arm.note.su_s_8ko_rocket: 80 mm HEAT: good penetration, little explosive. Needs precise hits on the roof or sides, around 6 rockets for an MBT.
arm.note.us_hydra_70_m247: HEAT with decent penetration and enough blast to knock out open-topped vehicles with near misses. Fire in bursts.
arm.note.sws_oerlikon_oe82: Among the best penetration of any unguided rocket; found on few aircraft.
arm.note.su_s_24b_rocket: Big HE rocket: imprecise, but its blast hurts light armor and groups of vehicles.
arm.note.us_zuni_wafar_mk32: Big HE rocket: imprecise, but its blast hurts light armor and groups of vehicles.
arm.note.su_rbs82: WWII rocket whose penetration now depends on its speed (September 2026).
arm.note.jp_type91mod2_torpedo: The most forgiving aircraft torpedo: can be dropped fast and relatively high.
arm.note.us_mk13_torpedo: Late Mk.13: easy to drop at fairly high speed and altitude. Early versions need a slow, low approach.
arm.notesHint: Summarized from the official forum, wiki and Steam discussions (October 2026); patches can make them outdated.
arm.colh.acc: Acceleration off the rail (first-stage thrust / launch mass): how fast it gets up to speed, key at close range
arm.fh.ccm_r: IRCCM: the seeker pauses when it sees flares, then looks again — flare and turn to beat it
arm.fh.ccm_g: IRCCM: narrow tracking gate that ignores flares off the target's axis — flares still work head-on or from behind
arm.fh.ccm_rg: IRCCM: flare rejection + narrow tracking gate — the hardest to flare
arm.colh.yld: Explosive energy in kilotons (kt) or megatons (Mt) of TNT
arm.colh.bh: The bomb detonates this high above the ground (air burst)
arm.useh.effn: Yield divided by the bomb's mass: the most power for the least weight
arm.nukeCustom: No aircraft carries it in game: mount it on any pylon in WTFTD (Loadout → non-standard weapons).
arm.guide.nuke:
Yield is the bomb's energy in kilotons of TNT: 30 kt is six times 5 kt, and the megaton bombs are in another league.
They burst in the air above the target: almost nothing survives within a wide radius, including allies.
Drop from high and fast, then turn away: the carrier aircraft can be caught in the blast.
In regular battles they're rare (a reward in high-rank ground battles); in WTFTD you can mount any of them on any pylon to test them.
arm.fh.iw: In battle, its explosion wins the match for your team: the nuclear killstreak reward of ground battles. The game files give it no yield.
myw.title: My weapons
myw.hint: Your own versions of the game's weapons: more explosive, more thrust, more G, a nuclear charge… Make one with Modify in the Weapons tab, then put it on a pylon: vehicle panel → Loadout → Custom pylons → click a pylon → My weapons. Single-player missions only (custom vehicles).
myw.empty: No weapon yet. In the Weapons tab, click Modify on a missile, bomb, rocket or torpedo.
myw.modifyHint: Make your own version of this weapon (My weapons)
myw.name: Name
myw.h.e: The blast radius grows as the cube root: ×1000 explosive ≈ ×10 radius. The explosion shown follows it.
myw.h.kt: Makes it a nuclear weapon, like the game's nuclear bombs (5 kt to 1.6 Mt). 0 = none.
myw.h.force: More thrust: faster, and farther with a longer burn.
myw.h.g: How tight it can turn (the missile and its guidance).
myw.editHint: Put it on a pylon from the vehicle panel (Loadout → Custom pylons → My weapons). In game it keeps the weapon's own name.
myw.noChange: Nothing changed: set at least one value.
myw.noBase: This weapon's values aren't in the game data. Update the game data (Settings) and try again.
myw.advHint: Every value of the weapon's file in the game, block by block. A changed value here wins over the Simple tab. Hover a value for what it does. Unknown effects? Change one thing at a time and test it in game.
myw.advSearch: Search a value (e.g. fuse, seeker, G)…
myw.advUnknown: {path} — value in the game: {value}. No description yet: change it and test in game.
mywk.mass: Weight of the weapon (kg). Heavier = slower, shorter range.
mywk.massEnd: Weight once the motor has burnt out (kg).
mywk.massEnd1: Weight after the second motor stage (kg).
mywk.dragCx: Drag coefficient: lower = keeps its speed longer.
mywk.CxK: Extra drag when it manoeuvres: lower = loses less speed in turns.
mywk.CyK: Lift of the body: higher = turns more easily.
mywk.WdK: Rotation damping (x, y, z): how fast it stops wobbling.
mywk.wingAreaMult: Wing area multiplier: more lift, tighter turns.
mywk.finsAoaHor: Largest angle of attack the fins can give, horizontally.
mywk.finsAoaVer: Largest angle of attack the fins can give, vertically.
mywk.finsLatAccel: Sideways acceleration the fins can give: with loadFactorMax, what limits its turns.
mywk.distFromCmToStab: Distance from the centre of mass to the fins (m): stability.
mywk.force1: Thrust of the second motor stage (N).
mywk.timeFire: Motor burn time (s). Longer = keeps accelerating, more range.
mywk.timeFire1: Burn time of the second motor stage (s).
mywk.startSpeed: Speed when it leaves the launcher (m/s).
mywk.useStartSpeed: Starts at startSpeed instead of the launching aircraft's speed.
mywk.endSpeed: Speed used for the game's stats (m/s).
mywk.minDistance: Arming distance (m): it does not explode closer than that.
mywk.rangeMax: Maximum range (m). In a seeker: how far it can lock.
mywk.loadFactorMax: Most G the missile can pull. 100 = very tight turns.
mywk.reqAccelMax: Most G its autopilot asks for: raise it with loadFactorMax for tighter turns.
mywk.propNavMult: Proportional navigation gain: higher = sharper, earlier corrections.
mywk.baseIndSpeed: Speed the autopilot is tuned for (km/h).
mywk.timeOut: Delay after launch before it starts guiding (s).
mywk.warmUpTime: Seeker warm-up time before it can be used (s).
mywk.workTime: How long it guides (s); after that it flies straight.
mywk.uncageBeforeLaunch: The seeker can track before launch.
mywk.breakLockMaxTime: How long it keeps going after losing the target (s).
mywk.lockAngleMax: Largest angle off the nose it can lock at (°).
mywk.angleMax: Largest angle the seeker can look (°).
mywk.rateMax: Fastest the seeker can follow a target (°/s).
mywk.minAngleToSun: Closer to the sun than this (°), it can be fooled by it.
mywk.prolongationTimeMax: How long it keeps aiming where the target should be after losing it (s).
mywk.rangeBand0: Lock range on a target's rear (engine exhaust) (m).
mywk.rangeBand1: Lock range on a target from any aspect (m).
mywk.rangeBand7: Lock range on ground targets / helicopters (m).
mywk.loftEnabled: Climbs before diving on the target (more range).
mywk.loftElevation: How high it climbs when lofting (°).
mywk.inertialNavigation: Flies on inertial guidance before its seeker locks.
mywk.inertialNavigationDriftSpeed: Drift of the inertial guidance (m/s): lower = more accurate.
mywk.reacquireTarget: Locks again after losing the target.
mywk.sideLobesSensitivity: Radar side lobes: how much ground clutter it picks up.
mywk.multipathEffect: Radar multipath near the ground: lower = tracks low targets better.
mywk.explosiveMass: Explosive (kg). The blast radius grows as the cube root.
mywk.explosiveType: Explosive type (tnt, rdx, comp_b…): sets its TNT equivalent.
mywk.explodeTreshold: Impact needed to set it off.
mywk.hasProximityFuse: Explodes near the target without hitting it.
mywk.rendinstDamageRadius: Radius that destroys buildings and trees (m).
mywk.splashFallBySquare: The blast falls off with the square of the distance (nuclear).
mywk.nearHitPower: Hit damage close up [damage, distance m].
mywk.midHitPower: Hit damage at mid distance [damage, distance m].
mywk.farHitPower: Hit damage far away [damage, distance m].
mywk.endHitPower: Hit damage at the end [damage, distance m].
mywk.midArmorPower: Penetration at mid distance [mm, distance m].
mywk.countPortion: Share of the warhead turned into fragments.
mywk.blocksThermal: The smoke hides things from thermal sights.
mywk.shellCollision: Can be hit by shells and other weapons.
mywk.thrustDeviation: Random thrust spread: higher = less accurate.
mywk.bulletType: Kind of projectile, as the game sorts them.
mywk.aiAirOnly: AI uses it only against aircraft.
mywk.aiGroundOnly: AI uses it only against ground targets.
mywk.iconType: Icon shown in the game (display only).
mywk.preset_cost: Cost in the loadout (no effect here).
mb.title: My battles
mb.hint: Your own results, read from the replays saved on this PC. Nothing leaves it, and other players don't appear.
mb.noGame: The game folder wasn't found: choose it in Settings.
mb.noReplays: No replay in the game's Replays folder.
mb.autosave: In the game, turn on Options → Replays and Spectator Mode → Autosave Replays: each battle is then saved, and listed here.
mb.limits: Turn on Autosave Replays in the game to list every battle. It keeps the last 100: to keep one, rename it in its Replays screen. The result is written only if you stay until the end: a battle you left doesn't count in the win rate.
mb.several: A battle with several vehicles counts for each of them: the replay doesn't say which one made the kills.
mb.skipped: {n} replay(s) not read: being written, damaged or of an unknown kind.
mb.tkHint: From now on, not on past battles: the game's log says who shot you down and your replay says which team they were on, so it takes My overlay on and Autosave Replays. Enemies are not kept, and this list stays on your PC.
ch.title: What changed
ch.hint: Everything that moved in the game's numbers between two versions: the official notes only list the key changes. Compared on this PC each time the game data is updated.
ch.mine: My favorites, saved and owned vehicles
ch.emptyHint: This page fills in after the next game update: WTFTD compares the old data with the new each time.
ch.back: This isn't a game update: the data went back from {from} to {to} when its source changed, one source being ahead of the other. These rows only undo the newer version.
ch.dmNewer: The community datamine ({dev}) has a newer patch than your game ({live}): one you haven't installed yet. No dev server is ahead of it.
ch.devNote: Your game ({live}) beside the community datamine ({dev}), a whole version ahead: the dev server's.
ch.devBehind: The community datamine ({dev}) is behind your game ({live}): no dev server is open, or it hasn't caught up yet.
ch.devHint: Compare your game with the community datamine's newest version: the dev server's while one is open, else the live game's, sometimes a patch ahead or behind yours. WTFTD downloads it (about 1 GB the first time) and builds it apart, in a few minutes. Your game data stays as it is.
ch.devError: The dev server's data couldn't be built: {e}
ch.devClient: Built from your dev server client: these are the dev server's changes, not the live game's.
ch.devIsGame: Your game is a dev server client: its data is the dev server's already.
ch.gameHint: Keep your installed game's data too: switch to it with the Data button at the top, or compare it with the datamine's here. WTFTD reads your game's files apart, in a few minutes.
ch.schema: WTFTD itself was updated between these two versions: a value it now reads differently can show here too.
eco.title: Economy
hg.hint: The game doesn't tell WTFTD what you own, so you mark it here: one click on a vehicle, or a whole rank or nation below. It stays on this PC.
hg.played: You played these: mark them owned?
hg.playedHint: Found in My battles. A rented or trial vehicle shows up here too, so nothing is marked on its own.
hg.every: Also premium, squadron and event vehicles
hg.tableHint: Owned / total. A click marks all of that rank and nation, a click on a full one removes them. The Total column and the All nations row do the whole line.
hg.noLineupHint: Give it a name and a nation above, then add vehicles from what you own.
hg.noneToAdd: No owned vehicle left in this nation
hg.farHint: 1.0 or more below the lineup's top vehicle: it can meet opponents 2.0 above it.
hg.planning: Planning: any vehicle of this nation
hg.rule.top: The lineup plays at its highest vehicle's rating, and meets lineups within 1.0 of it.
hg.rule.avg: Air Arcade: the average of the three highest aircraft (A/2 + B/4 + C/4), rounded up, and lineups within 1.0 of it.
hg.rule.each: Air Realistic: only the aircraft you choose counts, and it meets lineups within 1.0 of its own rating. Shown here for the highest.
hg.rule.naval: Naval: the highest ship counts, and aircraft more than one step above it can't be used. Lineups within 1.0.
hg.rule.sb: Simulator has no ±1.0: Air uses rating ranges and Ground uses lists of vehicles, both changing every two days.
hg.noVehicle: No vehicle in this lineup yet.
hg.noGoalHint: Add the vehicle you want: the plan counts what's left to research, without what you own.
hg.planHint: In order: what an earlier goal already researches is counted once. Modules and crew training aren't counted.
hg.hostNotOwned: Not marked as owned in My hangar: the game needs a vehicle you own.
hg.damaged: The hangar file couldn't be read: it's kept as user/hangar.bad.json and a new one starts.
mo.hint: Skins and sound mods for the game, from files you pick. WTFTD keeps a list of what it installs and only ever removes that.
mo.noSkin: No skin in the game's UserSkins folder.
mo.noSkinHint: Pick a .zip or a folder you trust: WTFTD works out which vehicle it's for, and asks when it can't tell.
mo.noSound: No sound mod in the game's sound/mod folder.
mo.noPreview: this skin can't be drawn here: normal paint shown
mo.askHint: The files don't say. The game itself goes by the name of the skin's .blk file.
mo.soundWarning: Sound mods come from third parties, not from Gaijin. The game warns when one stops working, can turn them off, and some game modes don't allow them. Turning this on adds one line to the game's config.blk, enable_mod:b=yes. Turning it off puts the file back.
mo.onHint: On: WTFTD added its one line to config.blk and keeps a copy of the file. Turn it off to put the file back.
mo.offHint: Off: the game doesn't load these files, and config.blk is as it was.
mo.onByHand: On, by a line of your own in config.blk: WTFTD leaves it alone.
mo.gameRunning: War Thunder is running: it may write config.blk back as it exits, so nothing changes until you close it.
mo.soundsOn: Sound mods on: they load at the next game start.
mo.soundsOff: Sound mods off: config.blk is back as it was.

uninstall.mods: Skins and sound mods installed by WTFTD
uninstall.modsHint: {skins} skin(s), {sounds} sound mod(s). What you installed yourself stays.
uninstall.modsConfigHint: {skins} skin(s), {sounds} sound mod(s), and config.blk goes back as it was. What you installed yourself stays.

cg.hint: Scored missions for any vehicle: a goal, a timer, a real win or failure. Create one, play it in Single missions, User missions, and your best time comes back here.
cg.how: A result is saved while WTFTD is open during the mission. With Autosave Replays on, the replay then gives the exact time: without it, a pause in the mission counts in your time.
cg.noResults: No result yet: finish a challenge with WTFTD open.
cg.range.rule: Destroy the {n} trucks from {near} to {far} m, within {time}.
cg.moving.rule: Destroy the {n} trucks driving {near} to {far} m away, within {time}.
cg.defence.rule: Destroy {n} waves of tanks of your battle rating, within {time}.
cg.gates.rule: Fly through the {n} gates in order before the timer ends.
cg.bombing.rule: Destroy the {n} trucks 8 km ahead, within {time}.
cg.dogfight.rule: Shoot down {n} waves of fighters of your battle rating, within {time}.
cg.evasion.rule: Stay alive for {time} against the missiles of {n} MiG-29.
cg.heli.rule: Destroy the {n} trucks from {near} to {far} m, within {time}.
cg.desc: {rule} Your time is saved in WTFTD if it is open.
